title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals are using generative AI to impersonate people and commit fraud at scale. Deepfakes and voice clones derived from social media are being deployed to deceive victims into sending money, particularly targeting immigrants in Florida and Georgia who are seeking legal services. This is impersonation enabled by AI systems that generate convincing but false representations of real people.

The failure is that these systems were built and made available without adequate safeguards against misuse. Voice cloning and image generation tools can be accessed and applied to impersonate specific individuals without their knowledge or consent. No technical barrier prevented criminals from harvesting audio and video from social media and using it to create synthetic communications in those people's voices and likenesses.

What is not established is the extent to which the creators of these AI systems knew they would be used for fraud, or what specific systems were involved in any given scam.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfakes and voice clones for scamming people out of money. The FBI reported that Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams in 2025, with cases ranging from a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants, to a Cobb County couple losing $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scheme. Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints totaling $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia had 71 complaints with $10.4 million in reported losses.

Scammers are using generative AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photographs, and research family relationships to make their schemes more believable. The FBI notes these figures likely undercount the actual problem since many victims never report being scammed. Authorities recommend people establish code words with family members to verify identity during emergencies, verify urgent requests by contacting people directly, and never send money based solely on phone calls or voicemails. Banks are urging customers to pause before responding to unexpected money requests and to verify communications through trusted channels.
